answer.rationale: Write-path p99 at 5x coincided with a release that landed ~30 minutes before the climb, while daily settlement peak is a recurring load pattern and therefore a weaker explanation for a novel 5x regression. memory_b1 is the closest prior: rollback of a bad build restored a write/checkout path without customer impact, so that is the one archive record worth re-checking before committing. Capacity (b3) remains a plausible alternate if the release is innocent, but adding headroom will not fix a defective write build and this window allows only one action. Circuit breakers (b4) are rejected because failing open/closed on payments can drop customer writes, which violates the objective. Read-replica routing (b5) addressed report/dashboard read load, not settlement writes; applying it here would not reliably clear write p99 and could endanger write correctness. Failover has no regional fault signal and is risky mid-peak replication. Scale is broad_rollout rather than a canary (b6) so the write path is not left on mixed builds during settlement. Settlement value is in play, so downstream risk is flagged, and it is still uncertain whether the release is causal versus saturation.
